title: From insight to action: improving infrastructure risk posture with Terraform and Concert
content:
Advances in AI are accelerating vulnerability discovery, uncovering previously unknown weaknesses and complex attack paths. Anthropic’s Claude Mythos cyber reasoning marked a major shift in the vulnerability landscape, demonstrating how frontier AI can identify vulnerabilities that have persisted through traditional testing and expert review. As discovery becomes faster and more sophisticated, organizations will face an even greater volume of findings to assess and prioritize. 

 But finding more vulnerabilities is only the first step. To meaningfully reduce risk, teams need a way to determine which vulnerabilities matter most and a repeatable way to take action to address them. For many organizations, that path from detection to resolution remains fragmented. Disconnected workflows, manual handoffs, and complex infrastructure environments make it difficult to understand what is affected, whether a vulnerability can actually be exploited, and what changes are needed to resolve it. Until teams can turn those insights into action, vulnerabilities remain unresolved and organizations remain exposed. 

 Improving infrastructure risk posture requires connecting vulnerability intelligence with the infrastructure context and governed workflows needed to act. In this blog, we’ll explore how Terraform and IBM Concert help organizations move from insight to action, connecting vulnerability intelligence, infrastructure context, and policy-driven governance as part of IBM’s infrastructure lifecycle management solution. 

The foundation for infrastructure context and governed action 

Before organizations can respond consistently to changing requirements, emerging vulnerabilities, or new operational needs, they need a trusted and repeatable way to make infrastructure changes. Without a common workflow for planning, reviewing, and applying these changes, organizations can struggle to translate decisions into safe, consistent action at scale. 

IBM Terraform has long served as the trusted foundation for defining, provisioning, and managing infrastructure as code throughout its lifecycle. By standardizing infrastructure changes through repeatable workflows, Terraform helps organizations establish a consistent operating model across increasingly complex hybrid cloud environments. 

At the core of Terraform’s value is the infrastructure context and governed execution it provides. Terraform configuration and state give teams a shared understanding of the infrastructure they manage, while capabilities like Infragraph extend that context into a shared substrate across IBM’s infrastructure portfolio. Accurate, timely context helps teams and agents understand what infrastructure exists, how resources are connected, and where changes may have downstream impact. Equally as important, Terraform provides the governed execution layer for acting on that context. Organizations can codify security, compliance, and operational requirements with policy as code, evaluate proposed changes against those requirements, and embed approvals and controls directly into their infrastructure workflows. 

Together, infrastructure context and policy-driven governance provide the foundation for controlled action at scale. These workflows become especially powerful when paired with vulnerability intelligence, creating a throughline from vulnerability discovery and prioritization to safe remediation. 

From vulnerability discovery to prioritized remediation 

As vulnerability discovery accelerates, teams are under increasing pressure to separate the findings that matter most from the noise and act before exposure turns into impact. The challenge is not simply finding more vulnerabilities, but understanding which ones can actually be exploited and determining what needs to be addressed first. IBM Concert Protect helps teams make that distinction, moving from discovery to evidence-based prioritization: 

Discover: IBM plans to bring Anthropic’s Claude Mythos cyber reasoning into IBM Concert Protect, extending discovery to previously unknown vulnerabilities, including weaknesses without existing signatures or CVE records. Mythos-powered findings are planned to enter Concert Protect alongside traditional scanner results, helping organizations expand what they can uncover without creating another disconnected source of findings. 

Validate: With capabilities such as Concert’s proof of exploitability, teams can determine which findings represent real-world exposure. Rather than relying solely on severity scores or exploitability predictions, the capability continuously correlates application, infrastructure, runtime, identity, network and business context to validate whether a vulnerability can actually be exploited within a customer’s environment. 

Remediate: Once teams understand what needs to be addressed, integrations with Terraform provide a governed path for making the required infrastructure changes. Teams can use established Terraform workflows to plan changes, evaluate them against policy, and execute them consistently across environments. 

The real value comes from connecting these stages into a unified, consistent vulnerability management workflow. This helps organizations mitigate infrastructure risk more effectively by uncovering more vulnerabilities, validating what matters, and taking action safely at scale.

Together, Terraform and IBM Concert help organizations connect vulnerability discovery and prioritization with the infrastructure context and governed workflows needed to act, creating a more complete approach to improving risk posture across the infrastructure lifecycle.
